## Cell Membrane

The **cell membrane** is a *selectively permeable* barrier. See [the textbook](https://example.com/book) for diagrams.

- Phospholipid bilayer: two layers of lipids with hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails
- Selectively permeable: lets some molecules through, blocks others
- Fluid mosaic model: proteins float in the lipid layer
- [ ] Review the cholesterol diagram

![membrane diagram](membrane.png)

## Osmosis

Osmosis is the movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from low solute concentration to high solute concentration.

| Condition | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Isotonic | no net movement of water |
| Hypotonic | water enters the cell, the cell swells |
| Hypertonic | water leaves the cell, the cell shrinks |

<details>
<summary>Extra</summary>
Cells in pure water can burst because water keeps entering.
</details>

## Steps of Cellular Respiration

1. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into pyruvate
2. The Krebs cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix and releases carbon dioxide
3. The electron transport chain makes most of the ATP using a proton gradient

## Active vs Passive Transport

Passive transport needs no energy and moves substances down their concentration gradient.
Active transport uses ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient.

### Examples

Diffusion and osmosis are passive; the sodium-potassium pump is active.
